newsitem.title: HONG KONG: We guard visiting President Jiang, say HK police.
newsitem.headline: We guard visiting President Jiang, say HK police.

text.p: Hong Kong police said on Thursday they had liaised with China's security forces on steps to protect President Jiang Zemin and other Chinese leaders during the colony's handover but local police were in charge.
The Hong Kong police would take the lead role in protecting the Chinese entourage, police chief Eddie Hui said.
"All the (security) work in Hong Kong is the responsibility of the Hong Kong police, be it before or after July 1," Hong Kong television quoted Hui as saying.
The British colony reverts to China at midnight on June 30, ending 156 years under the Union Jack flag.
Jiang, accompanied by Premier Li Peng, will lead the Chinese delegation to a Sino-British handover ceremony.
The police had received no request from Beijing to help Chinese officials avoid Hong Kong protesters, Hui said.

Hong Kong's pro-democracy movement has said it will stage a protest march on July 1, hours after China takes back the teritory from Britain, to test Beijng's pledge that Hong Kong's way of life and free expression will survive the change of flag.
China has promised Hong Kong considerable autonomy and the survival of its social and eocnomic system and basic freedoms for 50 years after the transfer of sovereignty.
Hong Kong's 27,000-strong paramilitary police force is regarded as among the best in Asia and the city is one of the safest in the world.
